correctness.rationale: Independent reconstruction from prime-power Ramanujan-sum arithmetic reproduces the factor identity. Mod p, Q_p(Y)(Y-1)^2=Y^p-pY+(p-1) proves Q_p=(Y-1)^(p-2); Frobenius and E(1)=p(p-1)/2 give exact shifted Eisenstein for every odd prime, including p=3 and a=1. This implies irreducibility over Q and Q_p and normalized valuation 1/d. The coefficient-ratio inequality supplies strict |root|>1; a direct real derivative calculation yields a unique negative real root; cyclotomic roots remain simple. The derivative-resultant calculation yields the exact discriminant, with its sign fixed by the unique-real-root argument. The embedded verifier checked 14 cases, 417 coefficient comparisons, 265 shifted congruences, and six integer discriminant evaluations; none is used as an infinite proof.

value.rationale: Prime-power Ramanujan-sum polynomials are a natural, explicitly studied family; knowing that 1-X^P divides them leaves their full rational factorization and residual root distribution undetermined. The joint classification is complete for every prime power: one noncyclotomic irreducible factor (odd p), explicit archimedean annulus, exact nonarchimedean normalized valuation and total ramification, explicit discriminant, and exactly one negative real root. The result identifies mathematically meaningful arithmetic versus complex root structure rather than an arbitrary finite example; the known input formula and limited incremental nature are expressly acknowledged.
